title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
claim: In a preregistered 960-day day-ahead backtest on GB national demand, the same honestly timed weather forecasts cut error for Chronos-2, Timestral-209M, TimesFM 2.5 and a weekly-lag regression, and the models' lead over the regression largely disappears once the regression has weather.
why_relevant: The design our benchmark mirrors: zero-shot foundation models against a lag regression on identical forecast-regime weather, on national load a day ahead instead of zonal load a week ahead.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: On three load datasets Chronos-2 is the most accurate zero-shot and fine-tuned when future covariates are known or well forecast, but degrades as the covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet holds up better.
why_relevant: Tests exactly our oracle-versus-forecast weather question for covariate-aware foundation models on hourly system load, at a short horizon.

title: Results: zero-shot forecasting models and GB electricity demand
claim: In a preregistered day-ahead test on GB national demand from January 2024 to October 2026, zero-shot Chronos-2 and Timestral-209M beat a weekly-lag regression by about 7% and 9%, short of the 10% bar set in advance, and TimesFM 2.5 was no better than the regression.
why_relevant: The first study of the series our backtest mirrors: the same three models and the same kind of lag regression and 10% bar, without weather, on national load a day ahead.
query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load, Chronos-2 with covariates gains substantially from task-specific fine-tuning and is strong at short horizons against task-specific deep learning models.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with exogenous inputs on US and European system load, the model in our primary comparison; the baselines are deep models, not a regression.

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
claim: In a pre-registered benchmark over four PJM extreme-cold events, 90% intervals of three day-ahead load forecaster families lose coverage inside the events and no conformal calibrator chosen without the target event restores it.
why_relevant: Pre-registered probabilistic load forecasting on PJM itself; day-ahead, classical models only, focused on cold spells.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: A live daily benchmark that runs eighteen foundation models, linear and boosted models and operator forecasts on one frozen information set with archived weather forecasts for six European zones; over the first 32 days the weather covariates lowered the error of each of the ten foundation models run with and without them.
why_relevant: Live, leak-free comparison of foundation models with and without the same forecast weather on zonal load; day-ahead and 15-minute, European zones.

title: Replication package for "Battery charging, demand statistics and the evaluation of U.S. day-ahead load forecasts"
claim: An audit of day-ahead load forecasts in EIA-930 data for 49 US balancing authorities traces deteriorating forecast scores to reporting changes such as battery charging counted in CAISO's published load, and re-scores benchmark comparisons with pre-specified analyses.
why_relevant: About the data source of our target series (EIA-930 demand) and how its definition changes can distort forecast evaluation; balancing-authority level, day-ahead.

title: Timestral
claim: Mistral's four open-weight probabilistic forecasting models (5M to 209M parameters, modified MIT licence) are reported to set the state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench and accept past, known-future and categorical covariates.
why_relevant: Timestral-209M is a runnable model in the spec that takes temperature; this is its primary source, with weights inside the scored window.

title: TimesFM 3.0
claim: Google's 330M-parameter TimesFM 3.0 forecasts multivariate series zero-shot and takes past and known-future covariates such as weather forecasts.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable successor to the univariate TimesFM 2.5 row on our leaderboard; the spec lists it as running with temperature through FoundationForecast.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
claim: Two open-weight models (102M and 256M parameters) condition on past and known-future covariates, rank third on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench, gain 6.3 skill points from known-future covariates over 30 tasks, and are among the most accurate on a Victoria electricity-demand backtest.
why_relevant: A new covariate-capable model the spec lists as running with temperature, with an electricity-demand backtest among its results.

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data
claim: Under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, TimesFM 3 beats a pre-specified classical ensemble by 16% MASE on post-release data including electricity load, but in two prospective weeks its point-forecast advantage on load is not confirmed and its 80% intervals cover about 70%.
why_relevant: Post-release and prospective evaluation of a model we can run, with electricity load among the test domains.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: An adaptive GAM in state-space form that aggregates weather forecasts from several providers improves point and probabilistic forecasts of French national load over single-provider inputs, most at the extreme quantiles.
why_relevant: Forecast-regime weather as the input to a regression-family load model: the strong classical side of our comparison.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels: Time-Series Transformers Outperform Established Methods
claim: Across a control area, low-voltage feeders and end consumers, Transformer models cut short-term load error by 6.6 to 10.7% against established methods; zero-shot Chronos-2 is competitive on two datasets but misses special events on the control-area data.
why_relevant: Load benchmark with a transmission-level series and zero-shot Chronos-2 beside trained models; short-term horizon.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Across four load aggregation levels pretrained MOIRAI and Chronos-2 beat seasonal naive and XGBoost, and rank-16 LoRA on MOIRAI Large lowers normalised MAE by 7.5% on average while updating about 1% of the weights.
why_relevant: Zero-shot and adapted foundation models on load from country to building level; the baselines are naive and boosted trees, not a weather regression.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: On UK and Swiss distribution data Chronos-2 has the lowest error in high-demand periods at every aggregation level, 20 to 51% below LightGBM and XGBoost on high-demand NMAE.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 against boosted trees on load, scored on peaks; distribution level and short-term.

title: pl-forecast-bench: a leakage-checked forecasting benchmark for the Polish power system
claim: A benchmark of day-ahead and intraday forecasts of Polish demand, wind, solar and price that fixes the data, publication-time rules, a 12-month test year and reference models including ridge, gradient boosting and zero-shot foundation models, with tests for look-ahead leakage.
why_relevant: Same ingredients as our harness (archived weather forecasts, as-of rules, regression and foundation-model references) on national demand, day-ahead.

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
claim: On two German district heating networks zero-shot TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 with ambient temperature beat all trained baselines on hourly 24-hour forecasts over a full year, under perfect weather with a separate sensitivity run on forecast weather.
why_relevant: Oracle and forecast temperature as a known-future input to two zero-shot models on an hourly energy series; heat instead of electricity, day-ahead.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one university building TimesFM 3.0 with covariates has the lowest error, about 43% below weekly seasonal naive, without a clear advantage over XGBoost, and covariates leave its overall error almost unchanged.
why_relevant: TimesFM 3.0 with weather covariates on electricity load; one building, day-ahead, observed weather.

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Türkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
claim: An archive of 759 training runs, sealed test forecasts and trained models for a study of national demand forecasting at several horizons with calendar, holiday and temperature information.
why_relevant: Multi-horizon load forecasting with temperature and calendar inputs and a sealed test set; national, no foundation models stated.

title: U.S. utility load forecasts filed on FERC Form 714, 2006-2025: forecast errors, weather-normalized outcomes, prediction intervals and capacity decision rules (code and data)
claim: Code and data that score the peak and energy forecasts US planning areas filed on FERC Form 714 against weather-normalised outcomes and build prediction intervals from past errors, including PJM's own forecasts.
why_relevant: US utility and PJM load forecast errors as a reference; planning horizons of years, not a week.

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: In a preregistered comparison Timestral and Chronos-2 without covariates have a zone-averaged MAPE 0.95 to 1.35 points below SARIMA and GBM baselines on 2025 data, while a 14-origin post-release holdout is reported as not determined.
why_relevant: Preregistered zero-shot versus classical comparison at a four-day hourly horizon with a post-release holdout; carbon intensity, univariate.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Across four foundation models and nine datasets the choice of calendar encoding changes zero-shot MASE by up to 9.9% on ordinary days and 83% on holidays within one model.
why_relevant: Bears on how we pass calendar and holiday covariates beside temperature to Chronos-2 and the other covariate models.

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: On a preregistered grid with exact counterfactuals Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 answer what-if covariate queries with the observational association, more confounded than regression.
why_relevant: Preregistered test of how the covariate-aware models we run use a covariate, set against regression; synthetic data, not load.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
claim: From the timestamps of 128,656 weather forecast runs matched to GB auction gates, picking the latest run issued before the gate selects a run not yet published on more than 99% of days for six of ten model configurations.
why_relevant: A direct check on our forecast weather regime: issue time versus availability time of archived forecasts.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: For French load forecast 1 to 48 months ahead with a tabular foundation model, selected economic covariates improve skill by about 20% over 2015 to 2025.
why_relevant: Load forecasting with covariates and a foundation model; monthly and daily resolution at horizons of months.

title: TimeH2O v1
claim: H2O.ai's 108M-parameter zero-shot probabilistic forecaster accepts optional covariates and reports state-of-the-art GIFT-Eval and fev-bench scores on its card, under a non-commercial licence.
why_relevant: Listed in the spec as running with temperature through FoundationForecast; the licence is non-commercial.

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
claim: A pretrained multivariate model trained with target, past-only and known-future covariate roles is reported first on fev-bench and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval.
why_relevant: A new model with known-future covariates; not among the models we can run today.

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: A 145M-parameter long-context probabilistic model released with its full training recipe is reported competitive zero-shot on GIFT-Eval and the TIME benchmark.
why_relevant: Listed in the spec as a univariate FoundationForecast wrapper.

title: PatchTST-FM-r2 (IBM Granite)
claim: IBM's roughly 385M-parameter zero-shot probabilistic forecaster is reported second among replicable zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, under Apache 2.0 and OpenMDW licences.
why_relevant: Listed in the spec as a univariate FoundationForecast wrapper with a permissive licence.

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
claim: The new TabPFN tabular foundation model is reported to beat TabPFN-3 on tabular benchmarks, with gains carrying over to its time-series forecasting harness.
why_relevant: TabPFN-TS takes weather as a known-future feature and is listed in the spec as a FoundationForecast wrapper; the report is about the tabular base model.

title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
claim: On data published after every model's release pretrained models win 5 of 7 groups, and the size of their advantage follows how familiar the domain is from pretraining, not seasonal strength.
why_relevant: Bears on our weights rule: a post-release window does not remove the benefit of having trained on the same kind of series.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
claim: On 7,200 simulated series under a pre-registered protocol neither TimesFM-3 nor classical methods dominates: TimesFM-3 is never more than 1.31 times the best method's error, while automatic ARIMA is 21 to 24% better on seasonal data with four or more cycles.
why_relevant: Pre-registered foundation-model versus classical comparison on data the model cannot have seen; simulated, 12-step horizon.

title: Foundations without Fundamentals: Zero-Shot Blind Spots in Time Series FMs
claim: On simple diagnostic series Chronos-2, Moirai and Toto often give poor zero-shot forecasts and under-use leading-indicator covariates, also on real sensor data.
why_relevant: Evidence on whether Chronos-2 actually uses a covariate, the mechanism behind our primary comparison.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?
claim: Of nine zero-shot variants from five families tested on German, Polish and Spanish day-ahead prices over 2021 to 2025, only the TabPFN models consistently beat two specialised price models statistically, and that lead does not carry over to battery arbitrage profit in every setting.
why_relevant: Zero-shot foundation models against domain-specific models on an hourly energy series; prices, not load.
query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models
claim: A benchmark of six zero-shot models on energy, traffic and finance data finds they beat statistical and supervised baselines but trade point accuracy against calibration, with patch transformers losing calibration at long horizons.
why_relevant: Calibration at longer horizons for zero-shot models on energy data.

title: A controlled benchmark of temporal dependence for day-ahead electricity-demand discrepancies in Great Britain - supporting data and MATLAB code
claim: A retrospective benchmark on 364 days of 2024 compares independent, Gaussian-copula and empirical ensembles of the errors of GB day-ahead demand forecasts, with frozen operator data snapshots.
why_relevant: Error structure of an operator's day-ahead demand forecast; not a forecasting model comparison.

title: Online Conditional Vine Copulas: Forecasting Electricity Demand
claim: An online covariate-conditioned vine copula beats unconditional Gaussian and vine copula benchmarks for joint net-demand forecasts in five GB regions.
why_relevant: Probabilistic regional demand forecasting with covariates; a statistical method, about dependence between regions.

title: gridload-compact
claim: A compact probabilistic model for German net load self-reports lower MASE than every reference model on the 15-minute 24-hour task over 52 rounds and a tie on the hourly 72-hour task, using load history, clock and holidays only.
why_relevant: A load-specific model with a three-day hourly horizon; no weather input, self-evaluated.

title: Thaki-EnergyLoad-Forecaster v0.1
claim: Three LightGBM models trained on the UCI electricity load dataset forecast one meter's load 15 minutes, 1 hour and 24 hours ahead with MASE of 0.52 to 0.78 on a 2014 test window, without weather inputs.
why_relevant: A released load forecaster; meter level, short horizons, no weather.

title: Zero-shot time series foundation models for statistical postprocessing of weather forecasts: how much training data do they replace?
claim: Code release for a comparison of zero-shot TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2, given the ensemble mean as a covariate, with trained statistical postprocessing of 2 m temperature forecasts at 49 German stations.
why_relevant: A weather forecast as a known-future covariate for zero-shot models; the target is temperature, not load.

title: sktime v1.3.0
claim: The sktime 1.3.0 release adds forecaster wrappers for TimeH2O and Tabby.
why_relevant: A second route, beside FoundationForecast, to run two models named in the spec.

title: sktime v1.2.0
claim: The sktime 1.2.0 release adds forecaster wrappers for Tafsut, TimesFM 3, TiRex-2 and t0.
why_relevant: A second route, beside FoundationForecast, to run the new covariate-capable models.

title: BQEB ForecastBench: Benchmarking AI Models for Smart Grid Forecasting Using BQEB-Data v1
claim: A benchmark for next-hour load forecasting in which linear regression scores best among linear regression, random forest and gradient boosting.
why_relevant: A load benchmark with classical models only, at a one-hour horizon.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: sktime v1.0.2
claim: The sktime 1.0.2 release adds forecasters for Moirai 2.0, Sundial and WindFM.
why_relevant: Library wrappers for univariate models already reachable through FoundationForecast.
